subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs Competitors — NovaHealth
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@novahealth.com>, Tom Lin <tom.lin@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: next steps and proposed test plan

Hi Emily / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we can scope the bake-off: 

Pain points you called out:
- High inference unit costs at current workload volumes (chat + summarization at ~1.2M tokens/day)
- Latency spikes on long contexts impacting clinician workflows (p95 often > 800ms)
- Need for private deployment option for PHI/regulated workflows

Goals / success criteria you emphasized:
- Achieve average inference latency p50 < 120ms for 512-token chat requests in production-like conditions
- Reduce per-token cost vs current provider by at least 30% while maintaining parity on quality
- Support private (VPC/on-prem) deployment within procurement/security constraints

Competitive landscape we discussed: you plan to evaluate Redwood, Competitor A (managed API) and Competitor B (self-hosted). Key decision criteria from your side: latency, cost, private deployment support, and integration effort.

Attached is the proposed bake-off plan and a one-page recap. I also uploaded a proposed mutual action plan to track milestones.

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm the test dataset and a small set of golden prompts (link in related links).
2) Redwood provisions a trial environment and runs a 72-hour load/latency/cost test using your sample traffic.
3) We share a results summary (latency percentiles, cost projection, quality notes) and a short live review.

Can you confirm the point-of-contact for procurement and whether we should include an NDA before sharing the full test environment?

Thanks — I’ll schedule the initial bake-off kickoff for next week tentatively (Wed/Thu).

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-bakeoff-plan.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.xlsx
From: Emily Carter <emily.carter@novahealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lin <tom.lin@novahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: next steps and proposed test plan

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- Priority metric is latency during concurrent usage (we see spikes when clinicians open multiple notes) — p95 target is <= 500ms, p50 goal is nice to hit but p95 is blocking for us.
- Cost target: ~30% reduction vs current provider as you noted, but we’re also looking at operational overhead (on-call, infra ops).
- Private deployment: yes, must support VPC + KMS integration. Competitor A cannot do VPC today; Competitor B can but needs more engineering effort.

Procurement contact: procurement@novahealth.com (cc’d). For legal, we prefer to have a standard NDA — I can send a short form if helpful.

We’ll confirm the test data this afternoon. Tentatively OK for kickoff next Wed (18 Nov) — Tom and I will confirm availability.

Emily
Director, Clinical Platforms — NovaHealth

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: next steps and proposed test plan

Emily — great, thanks for the quick reply and for looping in procurement.

We can accommodate p95 <= 500ms as the primary SLA target for the bake-off. For the 72-hour run we’ll capture p50/p90/p95 across the sample workload and include a cost projection for steady-state.

Action items on our side (attached plan updated):
- Redwood to provision a VPC trial cluster with KMS integration and a short-lived service account for your engineers.
- Run three traffic profiles (baseline, peak, and clinical-burst) over 72 hours; we’ll also run a quality pass on the golden prompts.
- Deliverables: redwood-bakeoff-results.pdf (latency/cost/quality) and a recorded walkthrough.

Can you confirm which environment you want us to hit (sanitized-prod vs staging)? Also, please share the golden prompts file or point us to the Drive link — I saw the related link you mentioned but don’t have access.

If procurement needs any preliminary pricing for the trial, I can provide a one-page estimate for approval.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
Aditya

Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: next steps and proposed test plan

Quick competitive notes from our side to help frame the evaluation: 
- Competitor A: strong managed API but does not support private VPC today — likely lower integration cost but fails the private deployment criteria.
- Competitor B: self-hosting offers the private option but requires custom engineering; tends to have lower list price but higher operational headcount.
- Redwood differentiation: unified runtime with a VPC/private option, out-of-the-box KV/prefix caching that improves long-context latency, and a cost-optimization toolkit (batching/quantization suggestions) we can apply during the trial.

Suggested success criteria (for bake-off scoring):
1) Latency (p95) — pass if <= 500ms; partial credit for < 700ms.
2) Cost delta vs incumbent — pass if >= 30% reduction.
3) Integration effort — pass if Redwood can present a working VPC trial with KMS within 5 business days.
4) Quality — maintain or improve F1 on the golden prompts vs incumbent.

I’ll be on the kickoff and can lead the test orchestration. Happy to run the live review with your team.

—Marissa
Competitive Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
